rationale: Exodus 16 is God giving bread to a large people in the wilderness: "Behold, I will rain down bread from heaven for you" (16:4, BSB), each gathering "as much as he needed to eat" (16:18). Matthew 14 has a crowd in an eremos place (14:13, 14:15; the BSB renders the one Greek adjective "solitary" and "desolate"), bread, and "They all ate and were satisfied." The motif is a recurring setting and theme, and the grade stays plausible because Matthew has no manna, no Moses and no quotation; a script search finds "manna" nowhere in Matthew's BSB, and the Septuagint's verb for being filled in Exodus 16:12 (plesthesesthe) differs from Matthew's echortasthesan. The explicit link is John's: the crowd there says "Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness" (John 6:31) after John's account of the same miracle. Named readers draw the Matthew link without a textual marker: Chrysostom (Homily 49) cites the wilderness question of Psalm 78:19-20, "Can He give bread also? Or prepare a table in the wilderness?", and Strauss sets the feeding beside Exodus 16 and Numbers 11:21-22, finding "a striking resemblance even in details" but a "chasm" between them "too great for the latter to have been derived immediately from the former."
